html:
The court historian, adviser and later grand vizier of the Mughal emperor Akbar. He lived from 1551 to 1602.

He came from a learned family at Agra; his brother was the poet Faizi. He joined Akbar's court in 1574 and became his closest intellectual companion. He shaped and defended Akbar's policy of "sulh-i kul", peace with all, which gave Hindus and other non-Muslims equal standing and drew scholars of many faiths into debate at Fatehpur Sikri.

His great work, written in Persian, is the Akbarnama, the official history of the reign. Its third part, the Ain-i-Akbari, is a detailed survey of the Mughal Empire: its provinces, revenues, crops, prices, army, coinage and customs. Historians still use it as a uniquely rich record of an early modern state.

His influence made him enemies, among them Akbar's son Prince Salim, the future Jahangir. In 1602, on Salim's orders, a Bundela chief ambushed and killed him on his way back from the Deccan.
sum: The court historian, adviser and later grand vizier of the Mughal emperor Akbar. He lived from 1551 to 1602.
